page.layout: One page of verse, set in italic, lines indented in couplets; no notes in the margins. Below the last line at the right: the catchword "Non".

p.i: Tunc omne terris omnibus heu genus Mortale tantis imbribus obrutum Una periisset forte, passim Victima nil miserantis unda.
Sed vir relictus coniuge cum pia est, Cultor supremi numinis integer, Arca capaci clausus aluo Cum genitis nuribúsque charis.
Successit istis orta parentibus Terras per omnes gens habitabiles Diffusa, Sol quacunque Mundum Limpidus irradiat patentem.
Lugenda chordis flebilibus mala, Irata summi dextera Iudicis Quae mittit, ut poenas nefandis Criminibus meritas rependat.
Concussa motu Gallia civico Paces quietas odit, & ocia Vicina turbat, quin ruinam Dum ruit ipsa alys minatur.
Sic tecta tectis finitimis metus Incensa magnos protinus afferunt, Casura sic damnum propinquis Arboribus meditatur arbos.
Nec sola bello Gallia concidit, Sed dira cunctos cladibus horridis Bellona mortales fatigat, Funeribúsq; cruentat orbem.

page.notes: The first word of the page is set with a large initial "T", read as "Tunc". The running head is set in small capitals and read as printed. The "q;" in "Funeribúsq;" is a doubtful reading of the abbreviation sign; it is kept as printed and not marked. The printed "alys" and "nuribúsque" are read as printed. The long s is written as plain s throughout. The verse is treated as one paragraph per sentence, as the stanza breaks are not otherwise marked.
